plan:
- Microcontroller: ESP32 for Wi-Fi/Bluetooth communication and processing.
- Display: Small OLED screen for displaying information or status.
- Input: Tactile buttons or a small joystick for navigation and interaction.
- Power: LiPo battery with charging module for portable operation.
- Enclosure: Custom 3D-printed compact case to house all components.
- Antennas: External Wi-Fi and Bluetooth antennas for improved range.

subSteps.title: 3D Print all enclosure halves and component mounts
Install M2 heat-set inserts into MCU standoffs, display mount, and RF module mounts
Install M3 heat-set inserts into the main enclosure bottom half for case assembly
Test-fit all electrical components into their respective 3D-printed mounts and frames
Solder power wires from the 3.3V regulator output to main MCU, OLED display, all buttons, Sub-GHz RF module, and NFC/RFID module
Connect LiPo battery to the charging module and its output to the 3.3V regulator input
Solder I2C data wires (SDA, SCL) from main MCU to OLED display and NFC/RFID module
Solder digital input wires from main MCU to each tactile button
Connect analog input for battery voltage monitoring from LiPo battery to main MCU
Solder SPI data wires (MOSI, MISO, SCK, CS) from main MCU to Sub-GHz RF module
Connect external Wi-Fi/BT antenna to main MCU and Sub-GHz antenna to Sub-GHz RF module
Perform continuity checks on all soldered connections and power rails
Mount main MCU to its standoffs in the bottom enclosure half using M2 screws
Connect LiPo charger to USB power to verify charging LED and battery voltage with multimeter
Verify stable 3.3V output from the regulator after charging module
Upload initial test firmware to the main MCU to test OLED display, button inputs, and battery voltage reading
Test communication with Sub-GHz RF module and NFC/RFID module via respective interfaces
Mount OLED display to its mount and secure into the main enclosure top half with M2 screws
Mount all tactile buttons into the button array frame and integrate into the main enclosure top half
Secure the LiPo battery in its holder within the main enclosure bottom half
Mount the LiPo charging module and 3.3V regulator onto their combined mount, then attach to bottom enclosure half
Mount the Sub-GHz RF module and NFC/RFID module to their respective mounts and position in the enclosure
Integrate both Wi-Fi/BT and Sub-GHz antenna ports into the main enclosure top half and connect antennas
Carefully close the main enclosure halves, ensuring no wires are pinched, and fasten with M3 screws
Perform a final power-on and comprehensive functional test of the assembled device

projectDescription: A portable multi-protocol hacking tool featuring an ESP32 microcontroller for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Sub-GHz, and NFC/RFID interactions. It incorporates an OLED display, dedicated navigation buttons, and a LiPo battery with level monitoring, all enclosed in a compact, 3D-printed case with external antennas for enhanced range.

assumptions: Familiarity with 3D printing processes and settings
Basic soldering skills for small components and wires
Basic electronics knowledge and safe handling of LiPo batteries
Access to a computer with ESP32 development environment (e.g., Arduino IDE, PlatformIO)
